This relationship is supported by two distinct pathways: one involving Pterulamide Iv and another involving Beta-D-Glucopyranosyl-(Z)-3-Hexenol. Both pathways ultimately point to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 as the target. The compound is identified as a target in both pathways, indicating a possible role in the transport of anionic molecules, which is a common function of this family of proteins. The evidence suggests that the compound may act as a modulator or inhibitor of this transporter, potentially influencing the transport of specific substrates. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as the scores are relatively low, but the consistency across different pathways supports a plausible functional relationship.
